title: /review-grok refuses symlink edit targets by premise, not by an edit-time guard
gh-issue-create.sh makes every issue claim a sweep filed it and a second auditor verified it
QuoteEndpointTests' problem+json check on the anonymous 401 is null-conditional, so no BFF test fails without UseStatusCodePages
OrderEndpointTests' problem+json check on the route-miss 404 is null-conditional, so a bodiless 404 passes
A_foreign_meter_of_the_same_name_is_not_collected cannot fail: the foreign gauges' failed reads emit nothing, so a name-match listener passes
Notifications' A_pass_that_throws_leaves_the_host_running passes when the send loop has stopped after its first failure

Shipping's FulfilmentWorker A_pass_that_throws_leaves_the_host_running passes when the loop exits after its first failure
NoCertificateBypassTests scans for "CertificateValidationCallback", which misses HttpClientHandler's ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback
A_slow_carrier_still_has_every_claimed_row_polled_in_one_pass passes when TrackingWorker polls its rows one after another
SmtpMailChannel reads every 5xx to RCPT TO as the recipient refusing, so a relay-policy refusal makes rows terminal instead of backing off
Notifications' GrantCheckedTokenCache misses a JsonException, so a non-JSON 200 from the token endpoint serves a stale contact uncounted
The BFF maps a buyer's disconnect during pricing, RpcException(Cancelled), to a logged 500
Shipping's GrantCheckedTokenCache misses a JsonException, so a non-JSON 200 from the token endpoint is never counted as a refusal
The checkout quote echoes the caller's currency casing ("usd") while Catalog and Ordering return upper case
Notifications' BackOffSql clears LockedUntil without checking the caller still holds the lease
AbandonShipmentHandler discards Shipment.Abandon's result, so the tracking worker logs and counts an abandon that changed nothing
Notifications' InboxFilterTests Eventually returns its last read on timeout, so the redelivery test passes vacuously on a slow run
Shipping's InboxFilterTests Eventually returns its last read on timeout, so the redelivery test passes vacuously on a slow run
Shipping's CapturedLogs discards every log scope, so the no-address-in-logs tests cannot see a scoped address
TrackingWorker's backoff write is unguarded inside its catch, so a SQL fault there is logged as a claim failure and skips the ladder
MailOptionsValidator never checks Mail:Security is a defined mode, so "2" starts the host and every send throws
A booking made while its order was voided gets one hand-back attempt, and a failed one leaves the carrier booking live with only a log line
FulfilmentWorker's backoff write is unguarded inside its catch, so a SQL fault there is logged as a claim failure and skips the backoff
ContactFaultTests' unreachable-owner test accepts any exception, including the host failing to start inside the asserted lambda
HttpCarrierGateway reads every 404 on the events route as "no scans yet", so a missing route looks like healthy polling until abandonment
ContactFaultTests' open-circuit test loops on a request counter with no bound, so a read that sends nothing hangs the run instead of failing
MailFaultTests' open-circuit test loops on the outbound counter with no bound, so a lost Unavailable count hangs the run
SendWorkerTests' "nothing is left for a later pass to send again" assertion cannot fail, because no later pass runs
Shipping's service-boundary gate exempts every "Shipping." reference, so a production project may reference Shipping.TestSupport or Shipping.OrderingStub
The closed-result tests read only public nested types, so a non-public third case of BookingResult or CancellationResult passes unseen
A_carrier_event_carries_no_link_of_the_carriers checks properties only, so a link added to CarrierEvent as a field passes unnoticed
Notifications' consumer-registration control tests a predicate the gate does not use, so it guards nothing the gate depends on
The BFF's "named in the failure" options test rebuilds its own chain, so nothing checks that the real host's start-up failure names the member
Shipping's consumer-registration control tests a predicate the gate does not use, so it guards nothing the gate depends on
Notifications' service-boundary gate exempts every "Notifications." reference, so a production project may reference Notifications.TestSupport
The deployed-realm gate never reads the worker service accounts' role mappings, so an over-granted shipping-worker or notifications-worker passes
shipping-svc and notifications-svc may configure and read every Common.Contracts exchange, wider than the contexts they consume
check_permissions.py bounds only write from above, so a service account widened to configure or read of .* passes the broker gate and its suite
ordering-svc's unanchored inventory-commands and payments-commands grants also reach those peers' _error, _skipped and _delay queues
shipping-worker and notifications-worker set fullScopeAllowed true with no scope mappings, so Keycloak puts no cap on what their tokens carry
The library Ingress renders for any chart with a Service, though its own header says only the gateway has one
The NetworkPolicy "every address" guard refuses only the literals 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, so two /1 blocks or an empty selector open the egress fence
No seccompProfile on the Deployment or migration Job pods, so they run Unconfined wherever the kubelet does not default to RuntimeDefault
No container sets readOnlyRootFilesystem, which the chart README calls the right posture and leaves as an open decision with no owner
read_admin.py accepts a realm-check credential holding realm-admin: the gate refuses one too narrow but never one too wide
The gateway's web-bff route is a bare /bff catch-all, so any signed-in caller reaches the BFF's anonymous health endpoints through the edge
The edge adopts any well-formed client X-Correlation-Id, so a caller can stamp its traffic with an ID already in use, the attack §10.4 names
The edge honours a client's traceparent and tracestate, so caller-chosen trace context reaches every service and is persisted in outbox rows
The gateway's anonymous rate limit keys on the full remote address, so an IPv6 client rotating through its /64 gets a fresh window per address
ThumbnailUrl accepts any http or https host, so a publisher can point the anonymous product listing at a tracking host or a cleartext image
The client-credentials token HttpClient follows redirects in all three hosts, so a 307 at the authority replays client_secret to another host
CachingTokenClient checks the discovered token_endpoint for scheme only, so a discovery document naming any HTTPS host receives the client secret
The customer cancel endpoint accepts the saga-only reason codes, so a customer can inflate the payment_declined and stock series of orders.cancelled
A carrier's tracking number is held only to length and visibility, so a URL in it reaches every despatch email from the shop's own sender
Notifications' contact read never checks emailVerified, and ADR-052 settles that only for the shipped realm, where verifyEmail is off
HttpPaymentProvider catches only JsonException, so a provider answer in an undecodable charset escapes classification, the metric and the kill switch
No service checks the broker connection string's scheme, so amqp:// is accepted in every environment, and no record decides broker transport is cleartext
Nothing caps the tracking events one shipment stores, so a carrier rotating event ids grows rows and per-poll load until the 90-day give-up age
docs/secrets.md names the carrier, relay and payment-provider keys as held credentials but gives no rotation procedure for any of them
docs/secrets.md cites No_client_secret_is_committed as the never-commit control, but no test by that name exists; the live one was renamed
The realm gate never checks web-app's PKCE method, public flag or redirect URIs, though it enforces all three on mobile-app and calls a wrong answer a live exploit
The realm gate judges four clients but never web-bff, so a deployed web-bff left public, with a browser or password flow, or without commerce-api passes
No host refuses an explicit Encrypt=False or TrustServerCertificate=True in its SQL connection string outside Development
AddRedisConnections passes any Redis string through with no TLS requirement, and no chapter or ADR decides Redis transport
Every broker service account holds configure and read on the whole MassTransit: prefix, so any one can read or delete every other service's fault exchanges
§15.1's config-only deploy sample writes a tag read from helm get values into GITHUB_ENV unchecked, so a multi-line tag injects job environment
The per-service Redis ACL grants SCAN and RANDOMKEY, which ignore key patterns, so each service can list every other service's key names, contrary to §8.1
Workload and migrator images are referenced by a mutable tag, never a digest, so an overwritten tag runs new bytes on the next pull
A product name is checked only for non-blank and length, so a publisher can ship bidi-override, zero-width and line-break characters to every buyer
CachingTokenClient reads token and discovery bodies with no size cap and trusts expires_in unbounded, so one bad answer pins an expired token until restart
The dead-letter runbooks have the operator type the broker password into an interactive heredoc and never source OPERATOR_PASSWORD, so it persists in shell history
§12 cites a host-level cross-customer idempotency test that does not exist, so nothing pins the subject-scoped key in the real pipeline
The deployed-realm gate turns the password grant off only on web-app, and never judges Keycloak's built-in admin-cli, which keeps it on by default
HttpPaymentProvider holds the provider's reference and decline code to length only, so provider-chosen control or bidi text reaches logs, the admin view and Ordering
§7's SQL-login provisioning sample puts sqlcmd variables inside quoted password literals and never says how they are supplied or escaped
The realm gate drops the device-authorization and CIBA client attributes before any check runs, so a worker client with either grant passes
check_contact_client enforces "no service accepts notifications-worker's token" only through scope lists, so a client-level audience mapper passes
CachingTokenClient copies the token endpoint's error member into its exception message unchecked, so arbitrary endpoint text reaches every caller's logs
The error-queue shovel sample stores the policymaker operator's password in a broker parameter, though the shovel needs only a narrow AMQP identity
§7's provisioning sample gives the runtime login database-wide db_datawriter, so it can rewrite dbo.__EFMigrationsHistory and steer the migrator
check_permissions.py reads only users and permissions from definitions.json, so an added binding, policy or shovel can route around per-service isolation unseen
check_permissions.py keys permission entries by user alone, so a second-vhost entry hides a broad grant on / and the broker gate passes it
The broker runbooks run queue reads and the destructive purge through kubectl exec rabbitmqctl, which needs pods/exec and the node's Erlang cookie
smoke.sh's "every ConnectionStrings value comes from a secretKeyRef" check pairs a row with any later secretKeyRef, so a literal connection string can pass
check_permissions.py probes each foreign namespace with one invented name, <prefix>Anything, so a write grant naming a specific peer exchange passes
smoke.sh's trigger-coverage check reads any list item after the trigger and matches /** by bare prefix, so an inverted or narrowed path filter passes
